baslik: The Solar Storm That Set Telegraph Offices on Fire
sonuc: caused sparks and fires in telegraph stations worldwide
tetik: a coronal mass ejection hitting Earth's magnetosphere
mekanizma: a geomagnetic storm inducing currents in long telegraph lines
ders: a storm of this size today could damage power grids and satellites
yanilgi: It wasn't just a light show. The same storm today could knock out power grids.
tartisma: Our world now runs on long wires and satellites. How ready are we for the next one?
basliklar: What the Carrington Event Would Do Today
The Solar Storm That Sparked Telegraphs
hook: The Sun set wires on fire
soru: Are we ready for the next one?
sahneler: In 1859, the most intense geomagnetic storm on record hit Earth.
Suddenly, telegraph stations sparked, and some caught fire.
Astronomer Richard Carrington had seen a brilliant flare on the Sun.
A burst of solar plasma reached Earth in less than a day.
It slammed into Earth's magnetic field.
Currents surged through long telegraph wires.
Auroras were so bright miners woke thinking it was morning.
Today, a storm this strong could damage power grids and satellites.

baslik: One Switch Left in the Wrong Position Released a Chlorine Cloud
sonuc: caused a freight collision and chlorine release
tetik: a siding switch left set against the main line
mekanizma: a misaligned switch diverting a train into a parked train and rupturing a chlorine tank car
ders: the NTSB pushed for switch position indication in dark territory
yanilgi: The crash itself killed few. The chlorine gas released afterward killed most of the victims.
tartisma: A brakeman said he might have made a mistake. How should one person's error be caught?
basliklar: Why the Graniteville Train Crash Happened
The Switch That Released a Chlorine Cloud
sahneler: At night in South Carolina, a freight train was diverted onto a siding.
It crashed into a parked train, and a chlorine tank car ruptured.
The switch should have been set for the main line.
A crew member later said he might have made a mistake.
No train used the line for hours to reveal it.
Chlorine gas spread through the town.
Nine people were killed and hundreds needed treatment.
The NTSB pushed for switch position warnings.

baslik: An Overheating Bearing and the Toxic Burn That Followed
sonuc: derailed a train of hazardous materials in Ohio
mekanizma: a bearing failure detected too late by wayside hot-box sensors
ders: railroads added more hot-box detectors and reviewed detector data handling
yanilgi: Sensors saw the problem. The alarm came only shortly before the derailment.
tartisma: Officials chose to burn chemicals to prevent an explosion. Was the controlled burn the right call?
basliklar: Why the East Palestine Train Derailed
The Bearing the Sensors Caught Too Late
soru: Was the burn the right call?
sahneler: A freight train carrying hazardous materials derailed in East Palestine, Ohio.
Suddenly thirty eight cars left the track, and several burned for days.
A wheel bearing had been overheating.
The train passed three trackside heat sensors.
The final alarm came shortly before the derailment.
Crews then burned chemicals from several cars on purpose.
Residents nearby were evacuated.
Railroads added more hot-box detectors.

baslik: The Cable That Sheared the Cable Car's Lifeline
sonuc: fell down a mountainside when its support cable broke
tetik: the carrier cable overlapping the support cable
mekanizma: the moving carrier cable shearing the support cable near a pylon
ders: the crash is still the deadliest cable car disaster
yanilgi: The fall wasn't the only killer. Many victims suffocated after the car was crushed.
tartisma: Only one passenger survived. How do you make a single-cable system fail safely?
basliklar: Why the Cavalese Cable Car Fell
The Cable That Cut Another Cable
sahneler: A full cable car descending from Mount Cermis suddenly fell.
It plunged down the mountainside, and forty two people were killed.
Its cables had overlapped near the first pylon.
The moving cable sheared the support cable.
The cabin dropped about seventy metres.
The heavy carriage fell on top of it.
Only a fourteen-year-old girl survived.
It remains the deadliest cable car crash in history.

baslik: The Skyscraper Whose Windows Fell Out
sonuc: lost window panes that fell to the street
tetik: thermal stress in stiffly bonded double glazing
mekanizma: repeated thermal stress and oscillation cracking over-stiff bonded window units
ders: every pane was replaced and a tuned mass damper was installed
yanilgi: The wind didn't blow them out. The bond inside each window was too stiff to flex.
tartisma: Engineers later found the tower could also have toppled in some winds. How many flaws can one building hide?
basliklar: Why the Hancock Tower Windows Fell Out
soru: How many flaws can one building hide?
sahneler: Boston's new blue glass skyscraper began losing its windows.
Suddenly huge panes fell from the tower to the street below.
Each window had two layers of glass bonded together.
The bond was too stiff to flex.
Repeated heating and cooling cracked the panes.
Plywood covered the gaps, earning the name Plywood Palace.
All ten thousand three hundred forty four panes were replaced.
A tuned mass damper was added to stop the sway.

baslik: The Arch Bridge That Fell Onto Fishing Boats
sonuc: collapsed onto fishing boats in the harbour
mekanizma: corrosion leaving cables with a fraction of their cross-section
ders: Taiwan reviewed bridge inspection and maintenance
yanilgi: The bridge was only about twenty years old. Its cables had lost most of their steel to corrosion.
tartisma: It had been inspected once. How often should a bridge be checked?
basliklar: The Bridge That Fell on Fishing Boats
soru: How often should bridges be checked?
sahneler: A steel arch bridge in a Taiwan fishing port collapsed.
It crashed onto boats below, and six people were killed.
A tanker truck was crossing when it fell.
The deck hung from steel cables.
Corrosion had eaten away most of their cross-section.
Only a quarter of the steel was left.
The bridge had been inspected only once.
Taiwan reviewed how bridges are inspected.

baslik: The Plant Where the Fire Exits Were Locked
sonuc: burned with workers trapped behind locked exits
tetik: a hydraulic line repaired with improvised parts
mekanizma: hydraulic fluid spraying near a fryer, vaporizing and igniting
ders: North Carolina expanded workplace safety inspections
yanilgi: The fire wasn't unstoppable. Workers died because the exits were locked.
tartisma: The plant had never been inspected in 11 years. Who should have noticed?
basliklar: Why the Imperial Foods Fire Was So Deadly
sahneler: Fire tore through a chicken processing plant in Hamlet, North Carolina.
Within minutes, twenty five workers were killed.
Maintenance had patched a hydraulic line with improvised parts.
It separated and sprayed fluid near a fryer.
The fluid ignited.
Several exits had been locked, including a fire exit.
The plant had never had a safety inspection.
North Carolina expanded workplace inspections.
